content:
The White Nights in Russia are a summer experience associated above all with the city of Saint Petersburg, when the twilight stays bright for most of the night around the summer solstice. The phenomenon is not confined to Russia, but it has become a well-known part of the cultural identity of Saint Petersburg, and it gives visitors long hours for walking along the Neva, visiting the squares and watching the bridges. In brief: the bright nights last roughly from late May to mid-July and are at their strongest around the second half of June. This is a natural window, not an event with a fixed date; the bridges, festivals and shows have their own separate schedules, which must be confirmed officially before the trip.

What are the White Nights?

In cities at high northern latitudes the sun does not sink far below the horizon for part of the summer, so the twilight remains clear and full darkness does not fall for many hours. In Saint Petersburg the sky at midnight looks like a prolonged sunset, which is why visitors can walk, take photographs and enjoy the riverbanks in soft natural light. This does not mean that the sun stays visible all night inside the city, nor that every night will be clear. Cloud and rain affect the view, so it is better to set aside more than one night than to tie the experience to a single date.

When do the White Nights begin in Saint Petersburg?

Period What to expect Who it suits
Late May Long days and the start of the late twilight Those who want fewer crowds before the peak
June The clearest period for night-time light A first visit and the complete experience
Early July Bright nights, but the light gradually fades Those combining it with the summer holiday

The best places to enjoy the night-time light

The banks of the Neva

A walk by the river gives a wide view of the sky, the bridges and the historic facades. Choose a well-known, well-lit promenade, and keep an extra layer of clothing with you, because the air by the water is colder than in the city centre.

Palace Square and the Hermitage area

Palace Square is a strong starting point for the early evening, and it can be combined with the riverfront. Do not assume that the museums stay open late; admission and booking times have nothing to do with the length of the day.

Vasilyevsky Island

The edges of the island offer beautiful angles on the river and the city, but the raising of the bridges may affect your route back at night. Check your route and transport before you stand on the opposite side from your hotel.

A river cruise

A river cruise can suit a family if the operator is licensed and the weather is good. Check the departure point, the length of the cruise, the life jackets, the seating and the policy on children before you pay.

Watching the drawbridges without confusion

The drawbridges are a famous part of Saint Petersburg's nights, but they operate on a navigation schedule that may change, and some openings may be cancelled or affected by the weather and events. We do not give a fixed time in this guide because it could become wrong; check the official source on the day you plan to watch, and decide your route back in advance.
  • Choose one bridge or one viewing spot instead of trying to chase several bridges.
  • Allow for the walking time after midnight, especially with children.
  • Keep a working ride-hailing app and a back-up plan for getting back.
  • Do not stand on an edge that is not meant for pedestrians, or in the path of cars, to get a photograph.

A suggested four-day family program

  1. Day 1: arrival, rest and a short walk near the hotel.
  2. Day 2: Palace Square and the Hermitage with a timed booking, then dinner and rest.
  3. Day 3: a palace or park outside the centre, then an early evening stroll along the Neva.
  4. Day 4: a light family activity, an afternoon rest, then a river cruise or watching a bridge if the children are able to stay up late.
For the essentials about the city, see the Saint Petersburg guide, and to plan the whole trip start from the guide to tourism in Russia.

Tips for sleeping when the night is light

Some travellers find it hard to sleep when the light stays bright. Ask the hotel about blackout curtains, carry a sleep mask, and do not stay up late every night. Children need a steady routine even if the sky makes it look as though it is still early.

Weather and clothing

Summer in Saint Petersburg is changeable and can bring sunshine, cold wind and rain on the same day. Wear light layers and comfortable walking shoes, and carry a rainproof jacket. Do not rely on a monthly average; check the daily forecast before a river cruise.

Prices and budget

The White Nights period is in demand, and hotel and tour prices may rise during it. We do not quote an old fixed price for a room or a meal, because the price changes with the date, the location and the type of room. Compare the full offer: the hotel, breakfast, transport, guide days, tickets and the cancellation policy. You will also find our guide to Russia travel costs: daily budget and prices useful.

Events: what to confirm before booking

The period coincides with cultural and sporting events, but the dates and admission conditions change every year. Use the official Saint Petersburg tourism portal to confirm the event, the date, the venue and the tickets, and do not build the trip on an old announcement.

Travel documents

Check the validity of your passport, the official entry requirements and the airline's conditions that apply to the nationality of each traveller before tickets are issued: citizens of the six Gulf states enter Russia visa-free. Arcadia organises the tour program, accommodation, transport and excursions; it does not sell or process visa services.

Frequently asked questions

Are there White Nights in Moscow? Moscow enjoys long summer days, but the experience known as the White Nights is associated mainly with Saint Petersburg and its northern position. You can compare the two seasons in the guide to the best time to visit Moscow. Are all the bridges raised at the same time? No. Each bridge has its own schedule and its operation is tied to navigation, so you should check the official information on the day of your visit. Is the experience suitable for children? Yes, as long as the program does not depend on staying up late every day. Choose one night for watching, with an afternoon rest and a clear plan for getting back. How many nights do we need? Four to five nights give you good time for the city and the night-time light without pressure. Add nights if you are combining Saint Petersburg with Moscow.
